articles.title: 'HK has key role in keeping global shipping stable'
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong will play an important part in keeping world shipping stable and fast-tracking the sector's green transition, said John…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong will play an important part in keeping world shipping stable and fast-tracking the sector's green transition, said John Denholm, chairman of the International Chamber of Shipping (ICS), in a recent interview with Xinhua.

"The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is a fantastic economic engine. I'm sure that Hong Kong, as a main port in the Greater Bay Area, will grow from strength to strength," Denholm told Xinhua on the sidelines of the World Maritime Merchants Forum 2026.

Hong Kong's commitment to free trade made it a popular place to do business, Denholm said.

It is also a staunch supporter of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea as well as the International Maritime Organisation's regulatory framework, which are essential to making world trade flourish, especially when heightened geopolitical tensions jeopardise freedom of navigation, said Denholm.

Denholm also applauded Hong Kong's pledge to advance the green transition of shipping.

The city aims to see the proportion of its registered vessels using green maritime fuels reach seven percent by 2030.

Denholm expects the use of green fuels to grow fast as the shipping industry is committed to achieving net-zero emissions by around 2050.

Hong Kong is poised to make green maritime fuel more available to the industry with the support of the world-leading shipbuilding capacity and green technologies of the Chinese mainland, according to Denholm.

In the first three quarters of this year, Chinese shipyards secured 81.8 percent of the world's new shipbuilding orders.

China also has the potential to become a major supplier of green fuel, said Denholm.

At the opening ceremony of the World Maritime Merchants Forum 2026 on Monday, Hong Kong inked an agreement with the Port of Piraeus in Greece to jointly establish a Green Shipping Corridor.

Denholm called Hong Kong's partnership with other ports to provide clean fuel a "fantastic start" to promote the green revolution. (Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: South China Sea code of conduct could depend on landlocked Laos: analysts
articles.excerpt: ASEAN meetings again ended without a code of conduct, and Vientiane might have influence in future negotiations.
articles.fullText:
Landlocked Laos could play a huge role in future negotiations between ASEAN and China on a South China Sea code of conduct, potentially tipping the scales for Beijing, but close ties with its northern neighbor do not mean that Vientiane is acting as a proxy to block negotiations, analysts told Radio Free Asia.
As the leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, concluded their summit in Manila this week, the bloc again failed to finalize the code of conduct, or COC – an agreement that would seek to prevent confrontations in the sea which is claimed in its entirety by China and in part by Vietnam, the Philippines, Brunei and Malaysia.
The COC has been in negotiations for decades, and hammering out the agreement during this week’s meeting was a priority for the bloc’s current chair, the Philippines, a country with an exclusive economic zone, or EEZ, that significantly overlaps the territory claimed by China within its nine-dash line. Philippines foreign minister Ma. Theresa Lazaro on Nov. 15 told reporters that about 80% of a draft of the code had been completed.
But the agreement will have to wait until at least next year, when the next ASEAN meeting will be held in Singapore.
The overlapping claims of China and the Philippines in the South China Sea.
(AFP) Laos as an ASEAN member state wields significant influence despite not having any claims in the South China Sea, as the bloc operates on a consensus system. Vientiane’s deepening economic and military ties with China could make it sympathetic to Beijing’s foreign policy goals, Joseph Kristanto, a research analyst at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, told RFA.
“For China, having a sympathetic voice within ASEAN could therefore be useful, particularly in shaping the language and provisions of the eventual agreement, rather than necessarily obstructing the negotiations outright,” he said.
Influence does not mean control
Kristanto said Laos could influence ASEAN’s collective position by objecting to clauses supported by claimant countries, but he cautioned against treating that capacity, or its growing relationship with China, as proof that it was exercising influence at Beijing’s direction.
“While its growing economic and military ties with China could give Beijing considerable influence, I’d say that currently there is insufficient evidence to conclude that Vientiane is deliberately obstructing the COC negotiations on Beijing’s behalf,” he said.
Laos also has interests that could limit its alignment with China, particularly its longstanding political and security relationship with Vietnam and its standing within ASEAN, Kristanto added.
Although the bloc’s charter establishes consultation and consensus as its basic decision-making principle, it also allows the ASEAN summit to decide how a specific decision can be made when consensus fails. Additionally, disagreements over sensitive issues can complicate a common position.
An Oct. 12, 2025, photo distributed by the Philippine Coast Guard shows a China coast guard ship, right, deploying a water cannon at a Philippine Bureau of Fisheries vessel near Thitu Island in disputed waters of the South China Sea.
(Philippine Coast Guard via AFP) Still, if in future negotiations China were to push for a less binding code and faced resistance, Laos could oppose ASEAN decisions or joint statements to help reshape the agreement, Enrico Cau, a Taipei-based independent security researcher, told RFA.
“Much like Cambodia, Laos seems to be closely aligned to China,” said Cau.
He explained that Chinese investment and expanding security ties support a relationship that also serves the interests of Lao and Cambodian leaders: alignment with Beijing could help sustain their governments and support development without requiring democratic reforms.
Cau therefore saw little reason to expect either country to make a fundamental shift away from supporting China within ASEAN. His assessment pointed to potential influence over future decisions, rather than identifying a specific Lao intervention in the current negotiations.
A different regional climate
Comparisons with Cambodia draw on the breakdown of an ASEAN foreign ministers’ meeting in Phnom Penh in 2012. The meeting ended without a joint communiqué for the first time in the bloc’s history after disagreements over South China Sea language. Manila accused Cambodia, then the chair, of opposing references to Beijing taking control of Scarborough Shoal, a maritime feature within the Philippines’ EEZ.
Cambodia at that time described it as a “bilateral dispute” rather than a multilateral issue involving the whole of ASEAN.
Phnom Penh continued to veto drafts of the communiqué that included mentions of the shoal, Manila refused to sign off on versions that excluded it, and the meeting concluded in disagreement.
The following year, the Philippines took the issue to an international arbitral tribunal in The Hague, which issued a ruling in 2016 that invalidated Beijing’s claims based on the nine-dash line. China has rejected the ruling and continues to control the shoal.
Although Cambodia blocked an ASEAN communiqué that would have criticized China in 2012, the bloc is less likely to criticize China these days, Chong Ja Ian, a political scientist at the National University of Singapore and non-resident scholar at Carnegie China, told RFA.
“Laos could take a blocking role but the context is somewhat different,” he said. “There is less appetite across ASEAN for criticizing Beijing today.”
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., center, and first lady Louise Araneta-Marcos, right, greet Laos Prime Minister Saleumxay Kommasith and his wife Alouny Kommasith upon arriving for the 49th ASEAN Summit, in Manila, Philippines, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026
(Ezra Acayan/Getty Images via AP) Unpredictability in the U.S. alongside China’s ability and willingness to exert pressure on ASEAN has made the bloc’s governments less willing to openly differ with Beijing, with the Philippines a notable exception, Chong said.
While most of the ASEAN member states have publicly stated their commitments to a substantive code of conduct, Chong questioned whether this was in fact the case. Some might wish to appear cooperative while remaining lukewarm about an agreement whose obligations and enforcement were unclear, he said.
That uncertainty could complicate efforts to distinguish Chinese influence through Laos from wider disagreements within ASEAN itself, according to Chong.
Both Washington and Beijing have in the past made efforts to secure Lao support for their respective Southeast Asia policy goals. During Laos’s ASEAN chairmanship in 2016, then-U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry visited Vientiane and emphasized ASEAN unity and maritime rights. Months later, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi publicly claimed support from Laos, Cambodia and Brunei for resolving maritime disputes through talks among directly concerned countries.
ASEAN Philippines: key takeaways
For future South China Sea negotiations, the analysts said that Laos’s role must also be judged against what an eventual code would achieve.
Chong said a largely declaratory agreement would likely have limited effects on China’s behavior at sea, meaning Laos’s actions might make less difference than the underlying weaknesses of the document. Cau argued that an initial agreement could still provide a foundation for improvements over time.
Kristanto said the central question was whether Laos could influence the substance of the eventual agreement, rather than simply delay its completion.
“After all, concluding a COC and concluding an effective COC are two different things, particularly when contentious issues such as its legal status, geographical scope, and implementation remain unresolved.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Declines in Asia as Nvidia results fail to reassure
articles.excerpt: Local and mainland shares were mixed at the start of trade on Wednesday as equities failed to capitalise on blockbuster…
articles.fullText:
Local and mainland shares were mixed at the start of trade on Wednesday as equities failed to capitalise on blockbuster earnings from Nvidia that soothed concerns about the AI boom, but have been overshadowed by the resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang who admitted to a bunch of extra-marital affairs.

In Hong Kong, Hang Seng Index lost 79 points, or 0.34 percent, to open at 23,428.

Up north, shares began the day higher with the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index up 0.33 percent while the Shenzhen Component Index opened 0.37 percent higher.

In a highly anticipated earnings release on Tuesday, US tech giant Nvidia said third-quarter revenue topped expectations and doubled to more than US$115 billion while net profit hit US$65.3 billion.

The firm also increased its forecast for next year's revenue, predicting 75 percent growth, compared with a previous forecast of 70 percent.

Still, despite the positive results, Japan's Nikkei average reversed early gains to trade lower, as concerns about the outlook for AI development in the US and Nvidia's leadership outweighed the chip maker's robust outlook.

The Nikkei was down 0.72 percent, after earlier rising as much as 1.3 percent.

The broader Topix also turned lower, down 1.02 percent.

Nvidia shares rose nearly five percent in after-hours trading after the chipmaker, seen as a bellwether for the AI sector, reported quarterly revenue above forecasts in its first earnings report since Huang's abrupt departure as CEO this month.

Also, Nvidia's leadership signalled they would brook no dissent in their plan to find a new CEO, rejecting a "Stand With Jensen" campaign from allies of Huang, even as the Wall Street Journal reported a regulator was probing Nvidia.

"The momentum in Japan that was lifted by a strong outlook for Nvidia did not last long. The market was concerned about the fate of Jensen Huang," said Kazuaki Shimada, chief strategist at IwaiCosmo Securities.

"And a possible slowdown of US data centre construction weighed on investor sentiment, while the market also wanted to wait to see how Anthropic's IPO would proceed," he said. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Xi urges efforts to build a prosperous Asia-Pacific
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping on Wednesday said China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with greater confidence…
articles.fullText:
President Xi Jinping on Wednesday said China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with greater confidence and resolve to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together.

Xi made the remarks in a keynote speech at the Apec CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen.

The president called for maintaining peace and stability – and building a bridge of openness and cooperation – for the Asia-Pacific to prosper together.

"Stability brings security; security brings prosperity," Xi said.

"The Asia-Pacific economy has maintained a stable and positive trajectory, becoming a key engine of global economic growth thanks to a long-term stable regional environment. The more complex the external situation becomes, the more resolutely we must uphold the post-war international order."

He said the region should support free and open trade and investment, adding that efforts should be made to eliminate trade and investment barriers to foster an open Asia-Pacific economy.

"History shows that openness brings progress, while isolation inevitably leads to backwardness. We must resolutely uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organisation at its core, support free and open trade and investment, and safeguard the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains."

Xi called for efforts to steadily advance the process of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific.

Xi stressed the need to inject momentum into innovation-driven growth, and that efforts should be made to develop sci-tech innovation partnerships, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and promote green and low-carbon transition.

He called on the region to expand pathways to mutual benefits and win-win outcomes to prosper together.

Xi said China supports the establishment of a world association for bay areas economic cooperation, so as to deepen exchanges and interactions among various bay areas and explore new paths of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation.

"The Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects."

He also urged resolving differences through dialogue and consultation, and addressing challenges through solidarity and coordination.

The president added that China's 15th Five-Year Plan presents a list of opportunities for economic growth of the Asia-Pacific and beyond, describing the development blueprint as an invitation for cooperation extended to the global business community.

China will provide the global business community with its super-sized, open market, broad development prospects, as well as a cooperative environment that promotes mutual progress, he said.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Pochettino ends USA tenure, heads to Manchester
articles.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino's reign as United States coach ended with a simple 2-0 win over Haiti on Tuesday, sent off in…
articles.fullText:
Mauricio Pochettino's reign as United States coach ended with a simple 2-0 win over Haiti on Tuesday, sent off in style by a Christian Pulisic bicycle kick as he heads to his new role at Manchester United.

Teenager Julian Hall also added his fifth goal from six games to secure an 8-0 aggregate victory in the Concacaf Nations League quarter-final second leg in Cincinnati, with Pochettino set to fly to England just hours after the final whistle.

Pochettino, who steered the US to the last-16 of a home World Cup this summer, picked a strong lineup for his swansong and his favoured stars appeared determined to wave their coach off with a win, beginning with high intensity.

A bright Weston McKennie missed two good early chances, before turning creator in the 25th minute for Pulisic's opener.

Pulisic stole possession on the halfway line and surged up the left flank before feeding the ball inside.

McKennie crossed back into the box from the right and Pulisic, running away from goal, improvised a bicycle kick over his left shoulder that bounced in off the far post.

Striker Hall doubled the lead in the 43rd minute. McKennie again provided the assist, chipping the ball over the Haitian backline.

Hall did well to trap the ball, chest it down and then lift it over the goalkeeper. The 18-year-old has scored on all four US starts.

After the break Auston Trusty had a header acrobatically cleared off the line by Martin Experience. Video replays seemed to show it crossing over, but no goal was awarded.

Defensive midfielder Sebastian Berhalter picked up a yellow for a sliding challenge that rules him out of the semi-final in March.

Alex Freeman, the 22-year-old defender given his debut by Pochettino who has become a stalwart at right-back, did superbly to intercept a clear-cut chance for Josue Casimir.

Hall's header in the final few minutes bounced off the crossbar.

The often emotional Pochettino, who had issued a message before the game thanking US fans "from the bottom of my heart", calmly applauded Pulisic's spectacular strike, before exchanging warm hugs and smiles with his staff at the final whistle.

More testing challenges lie ahead, with United languishing in 18th place in the Premier League and due to face bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday.

Pochettino is expected to head directly to United's Carrington training facility on arrival. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Springboks coach Erasmus handed six-game ban
articles.excerpt: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-game ban by World Rugby on Tuesday for outspoken criticism of officials…
articles.fullText:
South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-game ban by World Rugby on Tuesday for outspoken criticism of officials following a rare defeat for the world champions against France.

Erasmus questioned the decision by the television match official not to intervene on a series of French tackles during his side's 21-19 loss in Paris.

"If he didn't see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing?" he said in a press conference in Dublin on Monday, ahead of the Springboks' clash against Ireland this weekend.

The 54-year-old will be banned from "any match-day involvement" with his players and coaches and will not be allowed to even enter the stadium.

"The panel determined that the conduct clearly amounts to disrespecting the authority of the match officials by impugning their integrity," World Rugby said in a statement.

"Teams have access to well-established and supported channels and protocols for raising officiating matters before and after matches.

"Challenging a decision is not the same as questioning an official's integrity or making comments that expose them to personal abuse."

Erasmus is no stranger to disciplinary action for taking aim at officials.

In 2021, he was banned from all rugby activity for two months by World Rugby for an hour-long video criticising the refereeing in the Springboks' first Test defeat by the British and Irish Lions.

The following year, he received a two-match ban for a series of social media posts criticising officials in a defeat by France.

South Africa Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing.

"The organisation respected the process but had requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualise his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives," said a spokesperson for SA Rugby.

Erasmus could miss the final of the Nations Championship on November 29.

South Africa trail New Zealand by one point at the top of the southern hemisphere standings with one round of fixtures to go.

The other four matches are likely to be South Africa's opening fixtures of the 2027 Rugby Championship campaign, freeing Erasmus up to return in time for next year's World Cup in Australia. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Tech outage wave continues, as Trump says all is fine
articles.excerpt: Technology outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended…
articles.fullText:
Technology outages that shut down email for many companies and grounded thousands of flights over the past few days extended to the US National Security Agency on Tuesday, as US President Donald Trump's administration downplayed concerns about a broader problem.

The NSA said its network experienced a "temporary degradation" during routine maintenance, but that "mission-critical capabilities" remained operational. The series of disruptions to critical systems, which also touched the banking system on Monday, prompted even some Trump allies to demand more information.

"If this is all a coincidence, it's like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world," US Senator Josh Hawley, a Missouri Republican, told reporters.

Trump earlier played down the incidents, which raised questions of whether the government and private sector had moved too quickly in cutting tech staff.

"It's like when you're big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It's fine," Trump told reporters in Manila, where he was attending the Asean economic conference.

Technology-related disruptions have hit every weekday since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of its services, including email.

The next day, the Federal Aviation Administration called for a nationwide ground stop that lasted 4.5 hours, the longest halt to US air travel since the attacks of September 11, 2001.

The spate of outages included a United Airlines technology failure on Monday that delayed about 150 flights on the same day that a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted some banking services.

On Tuesday, Apple said it was working to restore its systems after an internal update caused an outage that affected customer services including iCloud and Apple Pay. The issue was not caused by a cyberattack, Apple said.

Insurance provider Marsh also said on Tuesday its clients reported 105 cyber incidents in the last two weeks of October – more than double the 48 recorded in the final two weeks of May.

Experts worry that AI tools are feeding a surge of cyberactivity, with cybersecurity companies regularly turning up examples of hackers using AI to launch scores of intrusions at once.

"The recent string of major disruptions across industries highlights how deeply interconnected our digital infrastructure has become, and how a single technical failure or software update can cascade with outsized effects across critical systems," said Cynthia Kaiser, a former senior FBI cyber official and current senior vice president of cybersecurity firm Halcyon's Ransomware Research Center.

The string of tech outages is likely due to issues emerging from system upgrades, US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said in an interview with Fox Business on Tuesday.

"We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack... And we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here. And we can be fairly confident in that," Clayton said.

He attributed the NSA outage to patches deployed for a PHP vulnerability discovered using AI last month – a bug that could let hackers remotely take control of servers.

"Everybody recognises it's time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they're not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected," Clayton told the "Claman Countdown" program on Fox Business. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Woods to return to PGA Tour after two years out
articles.excerpt: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he…
articles.fullText:
Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday.

Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6.

It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024.

The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance.

In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver's license suspended for five years.

Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired.

Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket.

He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond.

Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test.

Days later, he said he was "stepping away" to seek treatment and focus on his health.

Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland.

He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour's Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver's license being suspended.

Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Norway, Portugal into Nations League quarter-finals
articles.excerpt: Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback…
articles.fullText:
Erling Haaland fired Norway into the Nations League quarter-finals on Tuesday with a last-gasp penalty which completed a stunning comeback from two goals down to win 3-2.

Manchester City striker Haaland scored from the spot in the sixth minute of injury time in Copenhagen as Norway leapfrogged their hosts into second place in Group A, on head-to-head record as both teams finished on nine points.

Both teams ended the group stage six points behind winners Portugal, who got their first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era with a 3-2 success against Wales.

The winner was one of two goals from Haaland, who also started the fightback in the 37th minute – and had a goal disallowed – after early strikes from Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg gave Denmark a commanding lead in front of passionate support.

Haaland was given the chance to nick a spot in the last eight from the Danes, who only needed a draw to go through, after a handball from Joachim Andersen which was spotted by the VAR officials just as the hosts thought they had survived another in a series of scares.

Denmark had been on the back foot ever since Haaland halved the deficit when a howler from Denmark goalkeeper Mads Hermansen gifted possession to Martin Odegaard.

It was Odegaard who forced home Norway's leveller with six minutes remaining and set up a grandstand finish which was completed with Haaland's dramatic winner.

"This has been one of the craziest years in football I've ever experienced," said a relieved Haaland to TV2 in Norway.

Norway will join Portugal in Friday's draw in Nyon, where the four group winners will be seeded and each play against one of the four second-placed teams.

Haaland's winner made Portugal's win over Wales irrelevant to their group placing, but Carlos Forbs' classy strike in the 70th minute in Cardiff made sure of a positive finish for Jorge Jesus' team.

Forbs' first international goal decided a hugely entertaining encounter in which Wales, already guaranteed to finish bottom of the group, put in a performance which belied their position.

Wales will take part in the play-offs to decide the final promotion and relegation spots between Leagues A and B, and on Tuesday's evidence they have a fighting chance of staying in the top tier.

David Brooks quickly replied to Bruno Fernandes' superb opener for Portugal and Wales had their tails up when Sorba Thomas slid the hosts in front in the 40th minute.

But Pedro Neto, who was later sent off, almost immediately levelled the scores and Forbs decided an even contest and ensured Portugal would bounce back from a humiliating defeat at the hands of Denmark at the weekend.

"It's a special feeling; I won't forget today. The most important thing is that we managed to win," said Forbs.

"We needed the goal to calm the game down, and it just so happened that I scored."

Northern Ireland were promoted to League A for the first time after Justin Devenny's thumping strike gave his team the draw they needed against Hungary in Budapest.

Devenny, who plays for Stoke City in England's second tier, lashed home a beautiful strike in the 65th minute at the Ferenc Puskas Arena to level the match at 1-1 and secure a second successive promotion for Michael O'Neill's team.

"I feel amazing. I'm due one, that was my second for Northern Ireland. To see the game out, we dug deep and we've deserved it. We've had a great campaign and we can't wait for more," said Devenny to the BBC.

Republic of Ireland will join Wales in the play-offs after closing out Group B3 with a 3-0 win over 10-man Kosovo and moving into second place. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Jensen Huang won't be back as chief: Nvidia board
articles.excerpt: AI chip giant Nvidia does not plan to bring its embattled co-founder back as chief executive despite Jensen Huang saying…
articles.fullText:
AI chip giant Nvidia does not plan to bring its embattled co-founder back as chief executive despite Jensen Huang saying he was ready to return, the company's board chairman said on an earnings call.

"The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," chairman Harvey Jones said, adding that the board would not be addressing the circumstances of Huang's resignation on the call, and would communicate further when appropriate.

Jones' start to a call about quarterly results was a forceful response to a movement to bring back Huang, who stepped down last week.

With Huang gone, investors are eager for clues about Nvidia's future and strategy, from its commitments of billions of dollars to cloud providers, suppliers and AI startups to who will ultimately lead the world's most valuable chipmaker.

Shares of the company rose 2 percent in extended trading, after Nvidia forecast sales ahead of Wall Street targets.

"It's no surprise that they're doing very well, and there'll be people who will breathe a sigh of relief about it," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments.

"But the story here is very complicated, and it's hard not to factor that in as an additional risk for people buying stock."

Jones said the board had hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to help find a new CEO.

Interim CEO Colette Kress, who is also finance chief, kept her focus on financials and products in the statement accompanying results.

"Our momentum is real," she said, without addressing the leadership issue.

"Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track," she added, referring to the company's latest flagship AI chip.

Huang, the AI boom's most prolific salesman, resigned on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia employees.

Jensen Huang's exit ended three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia's chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties, making execution a bigger risk than near-term AI demand, analysts say.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of US$130 billion, plus or minus 3 percent, above analysts' average estimate of US$125.25 billion, according to LSEG data. Nvidia said the outlook assumes no data-centre chip sales to China.

Adjusted gross margin is expected at 71 to 72 percent, compared with analysts' estimate of 71.7 percent.

Anshel Sag, principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said Nvidia's outlook was "quite positive, albeit not as ambitious as in previous quarters, which many have already anticipated."

He added, "I don't think anything near-term will be affected by Jensen's departure. His executive leadership team is capable and has followed his leadership and executed effectively for years, reaching this point."

The board is considering internal and external candidates for CEO, with Kress seen offering steady leadership during the selection process.

But a growing "Stand With Jensen" campaign has complicated the search, and Huang said on Tuesday he would be "honoured" to return if the board deemed it best.

"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said in his first statement since his resignation.

Earlier on Tuesday, Nvidia's board created a committee on national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang's departure, as scrutiny grows over the chipmaker's national security role.

Washington has also tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to Southeast Asia and overseas data centres serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had pushed for greater chip exports to China.

Investors were already uneasy about AI spending after the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections fuelled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-centre expansion.

They also want to know whether Nvidia's next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular.

Nvidia's third-quarter revenue more than doubled to US$115.8 billion, beating analysts' estimate of US$109.1 billion. The company has topped Wall Street's revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters.

Adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9 percent from 73.5 percent a year earlier, also beating analysts' estimate of 74.1 percent, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps. (Agencies)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US stocks fall but Nvidia rebound lifts sentiment
articles.excerpt: US stocks extended their tech-driven slide on Tuesday, while Nvidia results after the bell lifted US equity futures. Stocks ended…
articles.fullText:
US stocks extended their tech-driven slide on Tuesday, while Nvidia results after the bell lifted US equity futures.

Stocks ended lower during the US session but later Nvidia forecast revenue above estimates in its first report after Jensen Huang quit as CEO, sending its shares up 2 percent after market hours.

"There is a hope that this recalibrates the focus back onto the here and the now, which is this idea that the buildout and the need for the AI infrastructure is not stopping anytime soon," said Nick Giorgi, chief equity strategist at Alpine Macro in New York.

But worries over the rapid build-out of AI infrastructure and risks associated with the nascent technology intensified ahead of Anthropic's mammoth IPO, expected on Wednesday, which is targeted to raise as much as US$1.4 trillion.

All three major US stock indexes closed sharply lower, with the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq notching their first four-day streak of declines since September.

"Every sector in the S&P is down," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at Wealthspire Advisors, in New York. "So clearly, it is a reflection of overall investor nervousness as opposed to being driven by a specific set of stocks, whether they're AI-related or not."

"It's a confluence of all of the events that are there, and it seems to be speculation-driven as opposed to fact-driven," Pursche added. "It's not all about Nvidia."

Economic data released early in the session showed strong underlying retail sales, weakening industrial output and rising import prices, largely driven by spiking petroleum costs. Homebuilder sentiment plunged to its lowest level since April 2012.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 848 points, or 1.6 percent, to 50,759, the S&P 500 lost 76 points, or 1 percent, to 7,340 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 181 points, or 0.7 percent, to 24,328.

On the sector level, software and services, airlines and banks were clear underperformers.

Software shares were broadly lower, with Salesforce, Workday Intuit and Adobe dropping between 4.3 percent and 9.5 percent.

Microsoft eased 2.3 percent, while AppLovin dropped 3.9 percent.

JPMorgan shares dipped 2.4 percent after the company said insider Bregje de Best would succeed Jeremy Barnum as chief financial officer in early 2027.

Fed officials are increasingly suggesting that stubborn inflation has made the central bank more open to an aggressive US rate-hike path.

Markets are pricing in a near-certain 95.4 percent likelihood of a 25-basis-point increase in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

On Wednesday, minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting could help illuminate the central bank's approach to near-term monetary policy. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
articles.excerpt: The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new…
articles.fullText:
The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration.

Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an extreme, prolonged drought in the Colorado River Basin has resulted in dangerously low water levels in the Southwest’s two largest reservoirs, affecting the availability of this power source.

Residents and farmers in the US Southwest, a region that includes Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of Nevada and California, rely on water that melts in the spring from snowpack in the mountains and is slowly allowed to flow south via dam releases. Snowfall in the Rocky Mountains provides about 85% of the annual flow of the Colorado River . And in recent years, the river has seen record-low flows.

Two reservoirs along the Colorado River, Lake Powell and Lake Mead, have struggled to stay above the minimum level required for hydropower plants. At the end of September, Lake Powell’s depth was 3,518 feet, less than 1% above the level required to run the water through turbines that produce electricity at the Glen Canyon power plant. The Hoover Dam power plant requires 950 feet in Lake Mead, and that reservoir was 9% above the minimum in September.

Together, the two plants produced nearly seven terawatt-hours of electricity in 2025, enough to serve over 2 million people.

Low water levels have been an ongoing struggle for the region, which has been in a drought for 27 years. Meanwhile, climate change is continuing to shift rainfall and snowfall patterns across the region and around the world.

The effects of climate change on hydropower aren’t entirely straightforward globally—some regions will see more rain and snow because of shifting weather patterns, while others are likely to see less.

But it’s playing a role for hydropower availability, according to one 2022 review study . Rising temperatures bring more droughts, warmer winters means less snow and ice to fill the reservoirs, and more variability in precipitation can lead to alternating floods and droughts, making the power source less reliable.

Hydropower production is likely to be at its lowest level in over a decade in 2026 and tick even lower in 2027, according to projections from the EIA.

El Niño could provide some temporary relief. Sometimes this weather pattern can mean cooler, wetter conditions for the southern US. Heavy rains brought floods to the region in October and early November, and the water levels in Lake Powell rose more than 20 feet from their mid-September low. But the water is still quite low, and it’ll take much more to help reservoirs recover from decades of drought conditions.

Even as a changing climate complicates the availability of hydropower, the decline in capacity could push greenhouse-gas emissions higher. In 2023, energy-related greenhouse-gas emissions rose by 1.1% globally. A worldwide shortfall in hydropower generation accounted for about 40% of that rise, according to a report from the International Energy Agency.

articles.title: Working Holiday Scheme signed
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong and Chile today signed an agreement to establish a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for their youth. Secretary…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong and Chile today signed an agreement to establish a bilateral Working Holiday Scheme (WHS) for their youth.

Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Chile Francisco Pérez Mackenna signed the agreement on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen. Chief Executive John Lee and President of Chile José Antonio Kast witnessed the signing.

Welcoming the agreement, Mr Sun said: “Chile is Hong Kong’s first WHS partner in Latin America. The scheme will provide young people from Hong Kong and Chile with opportunities to broaden their horizons and gain first-hand experience of living and working in a different cultural environment.”

Mr Pérez Mackenna said: “We are pleased to provide young people from Chile and Hong Kong with new opportunities to experience life in each other’s communities. Hong Kong’s unique blend of Eastern and Western cultures, international outlook and dynamic economy will offer Chilean youth an enriching experience. We also look forward to welcoming young people from Hong Kong to discover Chile’s rich culture, warm hospitality and natural beauty, thereby strengthening mutual understanding and people-to-people ties.”

Under the agreement, successful applicants can stay for up to 12 months in either Hong Kong or Chile. Participants may take up employment to finance their stay or enrol in short-term courses, subject to an annual quota of 100 places for each side.

This marks the 15th Working Holiday Scheme Hong Kong has established since 2001. Similar arrangements are already in place with New Zealand, Australia, Ireland, Germany, Japan, Canada, Korea, France, the United Kingdom, Austria, Hungary, Sweden, the Netherlands and Italy.

Over 109,000 Hong Kong youths have benefited from these schemes to date. Details on visa application procedures will soon be available on the websites of the Immigration Department and Chile’s National Migration Service .

articles.title: Alcaraz sweeps aside Tiafoe in ATP Finals opener
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz looked in ominous form on Monday as he began his bid to win the ATP Finals for the…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz looked in ominous form on Monday as he began his bid to win the ATP Finals for the first time by cruising past Frances Tiafoe in straight sets, 6-2, 6-2.

World number three Alcaraz took just over an hour to deal with American Tiafoe and show why he is the favourite to win the whole thing in Turin, where he was the beaten finalist last year.

Since returning in August from a wrist injury that kept him off the tour for four months, Alcaraz has won three of the five tournaments he has entered, most recently the Paris Masters.

Alcaraz, 25, can book his place in the semi-finals on Wednesday by beating Italian Flavio Cobolli, who in the absence of former world number one Jannik Sinner is the crowd favourite.

"Sometimes I feel really comfortable," Alcaraz said.

"I feel like I'm better than the opponent in every aspect of the game.

"If I qualify to the semi-final or not, I think it's a great experience, a great week, getting experience," he added.

Tiafoe had a nightmare debut match at the season-ending tournament, the 28-year-old having no answer to Alcaraz's speed and power.

Only briefly in the second set did he look like challenging his opponent, a seven-time Grand Slam winner, when at 3-2 down he wasted three opportunities to break back. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Palace appoint Thomas Frank as manager
articles.excerpt: Crystal Palace appointed Thomas Frank as their new manager on Monday, handing the Dane the daunting task of lifting the…
articles.fullText:
Crystal Palace appointed Thomas Frank as their new manager on Monday, handing the Dane the daunting task of lifting the struggling club off the bottom of the Premier League table.

The former Brentford and Tottenham boss succeeds Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week after 16 games in charge.

The Frenchman was unable to build on the legacy of his predecessor Oliver Glasner, who oversaw the most successful period in the club's history.

Glasner led the south London club to their first-ever major trophy, beating Manchester City to win the FA Cup in 2025, and won the Uefa Conference League last season.

"It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I'm really, really looking forward to it," Frank said in a Palace statement.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."

Frank, who has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal, enjoyed great success during seven years at Brentford, leading the Bees into the top flight for the first time in 74 years in 2021 and establishing the club in the Premier League.

His work in west London earned the 53-year-old a move to Tottenham in June 2025 but he lasted just eight months as Spurs struggled.

Palace hope Frank can rekindle the highs of his time at Brentford with similar resources at Selhurst Park.

"I'm delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace," said Palace chairman Steve Parish. "He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club."

Sage paid the price after four straight league defeats left Palace at the bottom of the table.

He was hindered by the departures of Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Daniel Munoz, who reunited with Glasner at Nottingham Forest.

Palace have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, shipping 24 goals in 10 matches.

They will be hoping for an instant improvement as they prepare to face relegation rivals Coventry and Hull in their next two league games.

They also sit 21st in the 36-team Europa League table with four games of the league phase remaining. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Germany run riot over Netherlands in Nations League
articles.excerpt: Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win…
articles.fullText:
Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday.

Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to shreds in the most impressive match of Jurgen Klopp's six-game stint as coach.

It was Germany's biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959.

"The game was outstanding," Klopp told German broadcaster ARD. "We scored unbelievable goals. It was just insane. A fantastic football match and a magnificent experience. I wouldn't have even dared to wish for all of this."

Klopp singled out Gruda and Scherhant, two players he has given their debuts, for special praise.

"Boy can those two play. But the amount of work they put in, it's immense. That's what defines a team, and plenty of others can play football too."

So often criticised for a lack of end product since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, Wirtz has scored in four in his past four games for Germany.

"We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second-half," Wirtz told ARD.

The Dutch defeat was the first since their coach Xavi Hernandez took charge but, despite Greece's 1-0 win over Serbia on Monday, they also qualified for the final eight, although the last German goal dropped them to second in the group.

The Netherlands offered little in attack after Germany's second and missed injured captain Virgil van Dijk at the back, with the hosts cutting through a flimsy defence at will.

"I'm really sad, because before the game I was really proud," Xavi told reporters.

"Today it was not about the football, but about speed and about (our) values."

"I want to say sorry to our supporters, because today we showed our worst face. It's part of the process... We need to keep going and work on our values."

Germany knew only a victory would give them a realistic chance of reaching the quarters, with coach Klopp describing the match as a "final."

The game, a rematch of the 1974 World Cup final won by Germany in Munich, began with both sides risk averse and reluctant to move forward.

The Dutch had the first good chance when Jurrien Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away.

Just after the half hour, the Berlin-born-and-raised Scherhant latched onto a cross from Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu but hit the far post.

Nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same blade of grass and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the post.

"I don't think it could have gone any better, to score the opener here in my city. I don't think I could have dreamed of better. It's unbelievable," Scherhant said.

The Germans continued their assault on the Dutch penalty area after the break, Wirtz adding another with a solo effort on the hour. The Liverpool winger dribbled from left to right and back centrally before lifting a shot in off the left post from the penalty arc.

Schlotterbeck headed in from a Gruda free-kick with 65 minutes gone.

RB Leipzig winger Gruda laid on another goal six minutes later when he tore down the right and found Wirtz, who hammered in off the bottom of the crossbar.

In his first Germany match on home soil and just his second overall, Gruda then added one of his own, tapping in a Scherhant shot which rebounded off the post.

"We don't mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz.

"We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Uefa backs France's Diallo to stand against Infantino
articles.excerpt: European football's governing body Uefa has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against…
articles.fullText:
European football's governing body Uefa has given its "unanimous" backing to French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino in March's Fifa presidential election, it said in a statement on Monday.

The body said that Diallo had been "invited...to stand as a candidate in the Fifa presidential election in March 2027" and that European national associations had "unanimously pledged their full support."

The deadline for rival candidates to declare themselves is this Wednesday, November 18.

Uefa, which boasts 55 member associations, said Diallo "has accepted the invitation to stand" and that his candidature is set to be confirmed at a meeting of the French federation (FFF) on Tuesday.

Under its Slovenian president Aleksander Ceferin, Uefa has led the opposition to Infantino since his announcement in late July of a project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino quickly abandoned the proposal in the face of widespread uproar, but Uefa has since gone to a court in Florida in an attempt to gather evidence for a potential complaint of "criminal mismanagement" against the Fifa president in Switzerland.

Uefa had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in the election, which will take place at the Fifa Congress on March 18 next year in the Moroccan capital, Rabat.

Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani had been mooted as a candidate, but the Canadian later announced his desire to stand for a new term as the head of his confederation, which covers North and Central America and the Caribbean.

The Asian Football Confederation, which consists of 47 member associations, announced last month that it was backing Infantino for re-election.

Diallo said in September that the FFF was withdrawing its backing for Infantino in the election.

"We believe that the trust placed in the Fifa president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us," he said at the time.

Diallo, the 63-year-old son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the FFF since January 2023.

He was initially appointed to the post on an interim basis when previous chief Noel Le Graet was forced to stand down following a series of controversies.

Diallo, from Saint-Nazaire on France's Atlantic coast, was then elected to the role by a large majority in June of that year, before being re-elected in December 2024 for a new four-year term.

Infantino, a former Uefa secretary general, has been in charge of Fifa since 2016. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Villagers in northern Laos are afraid to use river water after rare-earth pond spill
articles.excerpt: Government and Chinese-financed mining company say water is safe, but residents are skeptical after animal deaths.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Lao .
After ponds at a Chinese-financed rare-earth mining operation burst and potentially contaminated two rivers in northern Laos, villagers living downstream told Radio Free Asia they don’t think the water is safe.
Villagers in northern Laos fear using river water after drainage ponds at a Chinese-financed rare earth mine burst upstream from their communities.
On Nov. 1, several drainage ponds began to overflow at the Laos-China Rare Mineral Development Company North 2 Ltd. in Houaphanh province’s Xam Neua district. The water from the ponds drained into the Nam Vaen River, which flows into the Nam Xam River, which crosses the border into Vietnam.
There are approximately 18 affected villages that rely on the two rivers for agriculture, and this is the third rare-earth spill in the area after similar incidents in February 2024 and April 2026.
Authorities began an investigation on Nov. 4, consulting with officials from the mining company, who assured the government that the water was safe. But as early as Nov. 6, residents living downstream from the mining operation reported that fish were dying. Later, reports surfaced that birds and livestock like cows and pigs had also died. Authorities suspended mining indefinitely on Nov. 13.
A dead cow lies in the waters of the Nam Xam river in Houaphanh province, Laos, Nov. 13, 2026.
(Samakhom Khet 4) The local government should have visited the affected villages instead of just talking to the company, a resident of Muang Vaen village told RFA on condition of anonymity for security reasons.
“They say there is no contamination, telling the people to be confident that nothing is wrong, but right now, fish are dying in massive numbers,” the villager said. “They didn’t go inspect the downstream area where the incident happened – they didn’t come at all. They went to the site up at the top, listening to them, listening to the company at the project site saying ‘nothing is wrong, this and that.’ They’re just trying to keep people from panicking.”
During the investigation, the mining company told the government that the pond that burst was a natural water storage pond, not a chemical waste storage pond. The company stated it has repaired the water pipes and will compensate damages to two families whose rice fields were damaged, in accordance with the law.
The villager said the people still do not dare consume the water or even use it for household chores, despite the assurances from the provincial government that there is no issue and they can use the water as usual.
A map showing the location of the spill in Houaphanh Province, Laos.
(RFA) Shortly after the incident, an official of the Houaphanh Provincial Department of Agriculture and Environment told RFA that residents living downstream should temporarily stop using the water until inspection results are available and the problem is resolved.
Later, on Nov. 15, another official of the same department told RFA that authorities are currently investigating why the animals are dying.
“Right now, they have fixed it,” the second official said. “Currently, agricultural production can proceed, and the water can be used normally. As for the dead fish and other dead animals, they are still analyzing it.”
Foreign-invested farming, mining and development projects in Laos have sparked friction over cases of environmental pollution and land often taken without proper compensation, leaving villagers fearing retaliation if they speak out.
Skeptical residents
Residents have raised questions and demanded that relevant authorities conduct a serious investigation following state media reports clarifying that there was no chemical contamination of the water.
They also told RFA that they do not trust the Nov. 4 investigation, after which authorities announced that they found no severe impact and no dead aquatic animals, though there was still an issue with water concentration that might be caused by saltwater seepage from an old mining pit. The authorities at that time said they were waiting for official confirmation test results from the National Water Quality Research Institute.
But some of the residents have turned to mountain spring water, which is more difficult to collect, and is insufficient for their livelihoods, they told RFA. They do not trust the government because a similar incident occurred at the same mining operation in 2024. At that time the villagers tested the water themselves and found it was contaminated.
The rare earth mine developed by the Laos-China Rare Mineral Development Company North 2 Limited in Xam Neua district, Houaphanh province, Laos, is seen Feb. 27, 2024.
(Airbus) “Many villages are indirectly affected, so to speak – all 18 or 19 villages here,” a second villager told RFA on condition of anonymity to speak freely. “We cannot use the main river, the Nam Vaen.”
The villagers are demanding that authorities help them find replacement water to use for watering vegetables and agricultural production.
“Right now, for drinking and living water, it’s just mountain spring water and tiny streams, which isn’t enough to water vegetables and other crops,” the second villager said. “We are facing many hardships. They came to inspect and said nothing was wrong, yet we see so many dead fish there. Just like the previous time—when we took the water to get tested and we found contamination. When they took it to get tested, they didn’t find anything.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Unemployment rate drops to 3.8%
articles.excerpt: The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate decreased from 3.9% in the three months from July to September to 3.8% in the…
articles.fullText:
The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate decreased from 3.9% in the three months from July to September to 3.8% in the period from August to October, the Census & Statistics Department announced today.

The underemployment rate remained at 2%.

Total employment was 3,653,800, down 1,200 from the previous three-month period, while the labour force dropped by around 5,800 to 3,804,200.

Looking ahead, Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun said that the ongoing expansion of the local economy, solid consumption sentiment and continued growth in inbound tourism should render support to the overall labour market conditions.

“The Government will continue to closely monitor the evolving external uncertainties for their potential implications on corporate hiring sentiments and provide job-seekers with appropriate support," Mr Sun said.

articles.title: Lawmaker supports decision to cut short harbour swim
articles.excerpt: Legislator Vincent Cheng, who took part in Sunday's cross-harbour swim, on Monday said it was appropriate for the organiser to…
articles.fullText:
Legislator Vincent Cheng, who took part in Sunday's cross-harbour swim, on Monday said it was appropriate for the organiser to call off the last race on safety grounds.

About 4,000 swimmers signed up to this year's annual race from Wan Chai to Tsim Sha Tsui.

Cheng said safety was the top priority and the conditions at the time posed a certain risk and the last-minute cancellation was a responsible decision of the organiser.

He said the currents were very strong during the final 300 metres to the finish, describing the situation as somewhat dangerous and chaotic.

"Normally a usual swim is probably maybe about 45 minutes, half an hour, but yesterday I swam for one hour 20 minutes, and I was still at the Avenue of Stars there, so there is also a certain risk there," Cheng told an RTHK programme on Monday.

He suggested that organisers should give participants earlier psychological preparation if they know the currents are strong, and consider extending the overall race time next time.

He also proposed refunding registration fees to those affected or giving them the opportunity to rejoin next year, as well as reviewing the race procedures and arrangements for better forecasting.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Scotland fend off late fightback to beat Wallabies
articles.excerpt: Scotland survived a late rally to beat Australia 15-12 in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Sunday as the Wallabies…
articles.fullText:
Scotland survived a late rally to beat Australia 15-12 in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Sunday as the Wallabies suffered a fourth successive defeat.

The Dark Blues led 12-5 at half-time thanks to two tries from Matt Fagerson and Australia-born Jack Dempsey to one from Wallaby wing Harry Potter.

Neither side managed another point until fly-half Finn Russell's penalty six minutes from time put Scotland 10 points ahead.

But Max Jorgensen's 79th-minute try, converted by Ben Donaldson, gave the Wallabies hope of an improbable win before the recalled Scotland duo of Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn frustrated a last-ditch Australia attack.

Victory saw Scotland leapfrog Wales into fourth place in the Northern Hemisphere table.

Both teams arrived at Murrayfield with concerns over their defence.

Scotland lost 43-21 at home to New Zealand in their November opener last week, while the Wallabies went down 45-22 to England at Twickenham — the third match in a row where Australia had given up at least 40 points.

Scotland suffered a setback shortly before kick-off when captain Sione Tuipulotu pulled out because of a knee injury, with Tom Jordan taking the Australia-born centre's place in midfield.

Nevertheless, it took Scotland just eight minutes to open the scoring.

From a close-range scrum, the ball was worked to the onrushing Jordan and he found Ben White, with the scrum-half's pass releasing unguarded flanker Fagerson, who dived over out wide for his sixth Test try.

Finn Russell's conversion hit the post and just three minutes later Australia were level.

Scotland's defence was split apart as a delayed pass from recalled fly-half Carter Gordon and a missed tackle from Russell allowed Potter to slide over at a rainswept Murrayfield for a try Ryan Lonergan could not convert.

Scotland thought they had a second try when Kyle Steyn volleyed a bouncing ball forward from a grubber kick, with Darcy Graham touching down.

But the score was disallowed on review after Steyn was ruled to have been in touch.

But their second try did arrive in the 27th minute when back-row forward Dempsey — who won 14 caps for the Wallabies before changing allegiance in 2022— barged over with Russell adding the extras.

Australia then also had a try disallowed on review, with Billy Pollard's score from a driving maul ruled out for obstruction to leave Scotland 12-5 ahead at the break.

Pollard was yellow carded in the 46th minute for a head-on-head collision with Kinghorn but the Scots were unable to make the extra man count in a scrappy contest.

It was not until the 74th minute that Russell's penalty put Scotland two scores in front.

The Wallabies mounted a frantic rally which ended with Jorgensen speeding in for a try to give the hosts a scare before Scotland celebrated their fifth win in six Tests against Australia. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
articles.excerpt: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday…
articles.fullText:
Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday.

Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California.

Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament.

She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut.

"It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva.

The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success.

"I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself."

A grueling 1hr 48min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead.

Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2.

Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead.

There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up.

She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40.

A long forehand gave Svitolina the break to knot it at 5-5 but Andreeva hit back immediately with her third break of serve to regain the advantage at 6-5.

The Russian made no mistake when serving for the set for a second time, holding comfortably to go 1-0 up.

The second set followed a familiar pattern, with both players trading some brutal groundstrokes in a series of long rallies.

Andreeva broke to take the lead at 1-0 but Svitolina responded in a marathon second game, breaking back after converting her seventh break point to level at 1-1.

Andreeva edged back in front with a break to go 3-2 up and then held for a 4-2 lead.

The next two games went with serve to leave Svitolina serving to stay in the match at 5-3 down.

A fortunate net cord left Andreeva with three match points at 0-40.

Svitolina saved the first and looked poised to save another, only to hit a wide open overhead smash into the net to give Andreeva the win.

Svitolina, who had been thumped 6-4, 6-0 by Andreeva in the opening round-robin game of the tournament, took positives from her performance.

"After the first match I was not expecting to play in the final," Svitolina said. "Unfortunately it didn't go my way but I gave it my all." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: England topple world champions Spain in Nations League
articles.excerpt: England ended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches at 43 on Sunday, beating the world champions 3-2 on their own…
articles.fullText:
England ended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches at 43 on Sunday, beating the world champions 3-2 on their own patch, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to join France in the Nations League quarter-finals.

Thomas Tuchel's team win Group A3, level on 15 points with Spain, after the hugely impressive win in Madrid in which La Roja were for long periods made to look a shadow of the team which won the World Cup.

But the Three Lions ended up down to 10 men and hanging on by their finger nails before inflicting on Spain a first defeat in a competitive fixture since March 2023.

Asked by ITV whether this was England's best performance of his reign as coach, Tuchel said: "Under the circumstances against who and where we played, yeah."

"(We showed) what we are made of and what we can do," added Tuchel, saying his team were motivated by their third place at the World Cup.

"We are always ready to push our limits. We had our best result in 60 years and we weren't happy with it. It's impressive what we did in the last two camps."

Harry Kane put the away side deservedly ahead on the stroke of half time, netting from the penalty spot, his record-extending 93rd England goal.

Ezri Konsa struck just after the break before Ben White gave England a barely-believable lead in the 57th minute when he latched onto Jude Bellingham's pass and finished between Unai Simon's legs.

England needed that cushion. Moments later they found themselves a man down when Elliot Anderson hauled backed Lamine Yamal in the box, conceding a penalty and a red card.

Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the spot-kick with Spain's first shot on target to set up a grandstand finish and bring back memories of England's collapse against Argentina which cost them a place in the World Cup final.

Those jitters intensified when Nico Williams slammed home Lamine Yamal's inch-perfect cross with 15 minutes remaining, but England just about held out under a Spanish onslaught.

Sitting third in Group A1 ahead of kick-off and needing a win to qualify for the last eight, Belgium had their backs up against the wall when Francesco Pio Esposito volleyed Italy ahead in the 11th minute.

But Belgium blew Italy away in the following quarter of an hour, with Maxim De Cuyper and Nathan Ngoy bundling the hosts ahead before Jeremy Doku slalomed through the Azzurri defence and confidently shot home.

Mark van Bommel's team deservedly claimed a spot in the quarters and made sure the scoreline reflected the balance of play when one of many attacks against an open Italy defence ended with Diego Moreira slotting home with 10 minutes remaining.

A dismal night for Italy, who were top of the group after beating France last time out and just needed a draw to go through, was made even worse when Senne Lammens saved Esposito's weak late penalty.

"Nights like this can happen, unfortunately. These things can happen during a rebuilding process," said Italy boss Roberto Mancini.

"We're disappointed, but this is the kind of night that will ultimately prove useful to us."

France top the group after bouncing back from defeat to Italy with a 2-1 win over rock-bottom Türkiye in Bordeaux.

Les Bleus will head into the draw for the last eight, scheduled for Friday in Nyon, Switzerland, as a seeded team, a position that ensures they will host the return leg in March 2027 but could mean they face Spain.

An Emirhan Topcu own goal just after half-time and Eli Junior Kroupi's first goal for France were enough for Zinedine Zidane's team to prevail and take top spot in the final round of of matches. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Mainland uni applications to open
articles.excerpt: Candidates planning to enrol in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions can apply…
articles.fullText:
Candidates planning to enrol in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions can apply online from December 1 to 31, the Education Bureau said today.

The number of Chinese Mainland institutions participating in the scheme will increase to 169 for the 2027/28 academic year. Located in 21 provinces or municipalities and two autonomous regions, they will accept applications from candidates taking the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education (HKDSE) Examination in 2027.

The Education Bureau encourages Hong Kong students to study on the Chinese Mainland via the scheme, thereby seizing opportunities to learn about the country’s social, economic and cultural landscape, and to bolster their own development.

The bureau said it will continue discussions to enable more renowned Mainland institutions to participate in the scheme, with a view to providing students with multiple higher education pathways and opportunities to connect with the country’s development.

Students should review their submitted application details online before January 10, 2027, while those providing supplementary information should do so before January 23. Students who pass the application verification process should pay the enrolment fee by January 31.

Institutions will announce admission results in late July next year. They may also arrange for supplementary enrolment depending on the enrolment situation.

articles.title: Australia down NZ to clinch Rugby League World Cup
articles.excerpt: Slick Australia overpowered New Zealand 32-12 in a pulsating battle on Sunday to lift a fourth consecutive Rugby League World…
articles.fullText:
Slick Australia overpowered New Zealand 32-12 in a pulsating battle on Sunday to lift a fourth consecutive Rugby League World Cup crown and reinforce their status as the sport's global powerhouse.

The home team took a 24-6 advantage into the break on a muggy evening at a sold-out Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane and never relented to inflict more pain on their arch-rivals.

Liam Martin and Jack Bostock bagged two tries each with Bradman Best and Tom Trbojevic also crossing in a fast and furious clash where Australia's fitness in draining conditions proved decisive.

The masterclass denied New Zealand their first title since 2008.

That upset – also in Brisbane – was the last time a team other than Australia lifted the silverware.

Since then the Kangaroos have won 23 games in a row at the tournament with Sunday's victory their 13th title from 17 World Cups played since its inception in 1954.

So dominant are they that they have lost just one of 20 Tests in the 2020s.

New Zealand performed an emotive haka, eager for revenge after going down 24-22 to Australia in an epic tournament opener over a month ago.

But they were immediately on the back foot, conceding after just 84 seconds.

Harry Grant threw a dummy and found big back-rower Martin who charged over with Cameron Munster adding the extras for a dream start.

After their shaky opening, the Kiwis knuckled down and after a sustained period of pressure centre Casey McLean stepped inside two Australian players to dot down and get them back in the contest.

Jamayne Isaako booted the conversion to move to 227 points, surpassing Shaun Johnson to become New Zealand's most prolific points scorer.

But Australia quickly restored order, with a beautiful offload from Best to Bostock in space who crossed in the corner.

Munster fluffed the conversion but made amends minutes later with a successful penalty to move Australia into a 12-6 lead.

The hosts were well on top and pierced a battered Kiwi defence again as Best finished under the posts before Martin collected his second just before the break with New Zealand tiring.

The second-half started where the first left off, with Australia's Trbojevic over after just four minutes, courtesy of Reece Walsh beating three defenders before the offload.

New Zealand were on the ropes with nothing going their way, including a try given by the referee then denied on review for a knock on.

But New Zealand persisted and Isaiah Papali'i split the defence for a converted try to leave them trailing 28-10 with 13 minutes remaining, only for Australia to hold firm with Bostock grabbing his second as the clock ticked down. (AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Exclusive: Internal ledgers show how Pyongyang steals wages from its workers in China
articles.excerpt: Paper trail obtained by RFA confirms to the outside world that Pyongyang takes a cut of about 90%.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean

[Editor's Note] Radio Free Asia recently obtained internal documents, on-site videos, and photos from a North Korean overseas dispatch company that has sent laborers to China. Most of these materials were produced in the first half of 2025 and include contracts between North Korean and Chinese companies as well as details on the “application of employee living expenses,” which is how their wages are classified. RFA has also secured a significant number of videos and photos of North Korean workers employed at Chinese companies. RFA’s analysis of these materials presents a harsh reality for these workers that includes stolen pay and poor working conditions. To protect sources, some parts of the documents will be redacted, and only selected scenes from the videos will be released as still images.

The North Korean government confiscates around 90% of the wages earned by workers it dispatches to China, internal documents obtained by Radio Free Asia revealed.
Sources in China have previously told RFA that the North Korean companies that handle the dispatched workers in China collect their wages and forward most of the money to Pyongyang in the form of “ loyalty funds ,” extra support for state projects, and other fees.
According to the sources, a Chinese company will typically pay around 2,500 to 4,000 yuan (about US$375 to $600) per month for every North Korean dispatched worker, but the worker will actually only receive 100 to 300 yuan ($15 to $45).
But the documents – which were made in early 2025 – include contracts, ledgers and other accounting records and are the first known instance where the deductions for the state are confirmed in print.
One contract, between a clothing company in China’s Liaoning province and a North Korean worker dispatch agency shows the details regarding the workers’ wages:
A contract signed in May 2025 between a clothing company in China's Liaoning Province and a North Korean overseas dispatch agency.
